newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil central bank changes show continuity - Malan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil central bank changes show continuity - Malan.

text.p: Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan said Gustavo Franco's nomination as the new central bank chief confirms the government's commitment to its current economic policy, local television reported.
"Franco's nomination is the guarantee of the continuity," Malan told TV Globo on Wednesday.
Central bank international affairs director Franco has been nominated as the new bank president after bank chief Gustavo Loyola announced his resignation on Tuesday.
Malan also said that the current foreign exchange policy of gradually depreciating the real would be maintained, sending a clear message that the currency will remain strong.
"There must be no doubts about that. There will be no maxidevaluation in Brazil," he told the television station.
Responding to critics of Brazil's maintenance of an overvalued currency, Malan said the country was now on the way to devaluing the real at a rate slightly above inflation.
"We are at the moment on the path to a series of devaluations slightly above inflation measured by wholesale price indices," he said.
Malan also shrugged off market comments that Franco's designation strenghtened him and his economic team.
"Over all these years, we never lacked broad and unconditional support from the president (Fernando Henrique Cardoso). We never felt weakened," he said.
Franco is seen as one of the "fathers" of the three-year-old Real stabilization plan and has been the force behind Brazil's foreign exchange policy.
Questioned whether there will be further changes in the Central Bank, Malan said he and Cardoso do not wish for the resignation of any other Central Bank directors.
He also said he and the bank's board will choose the new international affairs director in coming days.
